source_refs.note: Topic 18.10 (PDF 33); an original diagram of the potentials used in this section is added.

blocks.text: Transition elements can exist in several oxidation states, so they take part in many redox reactions. Whether a redox reaction is feasible is decided by comparing the standard electrode potentials (E) of the half-reactions: E cell = E(reduction) - E(oxidation), and the reaction is feasible if E cell is positive. In practice, the species with the more positive E value is reduced (gains electrons) and the one with the less positive value is oxidised (loses electrons).

blocks.alt: A vertical scale of standard electrode potentials: MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn2+ + 4H2O at +1.52 V, Fe3+ + e- -> Fe2+ at +0.77 V, 1/2 I2 + e- -> I- at +0.54 V and Cu2+ + e- -> Cu+ at +0.15 V. The oxidising agent gets stronger upwards. A box gives E cell = 1.52 - 0.77 = +0.75 V for MnO4- with Fe2+, and 0.15 - 0.54 = -0.39 V for Cu2+ with I-.
blocks.caption: The electrode potentials used in topics 18.10.1 to 18.10.3 (original diagram for this topic).
blocks.long_description: Half-reactions are written as reductions. The higher the E value, the more readily the species on the left is reduced, so it is a stronger oxidising agent. A reaction is feasible when E cell = E(reduction) - E(oxidation) is positive: MnO4- (+1.52 V) can oxidise Fe2+ (+0.77 V). Cu2+ (+0.15 V) should not oxidise I- (+0.54 V), but the reaction goes because copper(I) iodide precipitates.

blocks.prompt: A reaction has E cell = +0.75 V. Is it feasible?
blocks.explanation: Yes; a positive E cell means the reaction is feasible under standard conditions.

items: E cell = E(reduction) - E(oxidation); positive means feasible.
The more positive E: reduced; the less positive: oxidised.
